archival_memory.research_experience: I've been involved in undergrad research since the end of my sophomore year. It's been an eye-opening experience that has given me a glimpse into how knowledge is created in the tech world. I was initially hesitant, but it turned out to be a great decision.
archival_memory.research_lab: The lab I'm in is an interdisciplinary space where computer scientists partner with scientists from various backgrounds to make massive amounts of data more comprehensible. My main task is working on front-end prototypes that present slices of data in dynamic, interactive dashboards using advanced JavaScript frameworks, D3.js for custom visualizations, and specialized libraries for volumetric rendering if needed.
archival_memory.first_research_project: My first research project involved visualizing oceanic temperature changes over time for a climate study group. I wrote scripts to clean and unify the data, built a pipeline for near real-time updates, and designed interfaces for researchers to zoom into specific regions or timeframes. I co-authored a paper on this system, which was a surreal and proudest moment in college.
archival_memory.current_research: I'm currently working on immersive analytics platforms, exploring how VR or AR technologies can help scientists gain a more intuitive understanding of complex data. It's a leap from traditional coding and data visualization. I'm experimenting with integrating VR headsets, using engines like Unity or Unreal, and finding efficient ways to stream data into 3D environments. It's cutting-edge, but it's also exciting to forge my own path in this uncharted territory.
archival_memory.research_life: Research life is not just about coding; it's also about reading and staying up-to-date with the latest developments in the field. I spend a significant amount of time combing through academic papers, conference proceedings, and workshops to find relevant information that can help me solve complex problems. It can be overwhelming at times, but with practice, I've learned how to effectively skim through papers and extract the essential information. Sharing interesting discoveries with the lab and discussing how to incorporate new techniques into our workflow is a great way to collaborate and improve our research.
archival_memory.interactions_with_grad_students: I have the opportunity to interact with graduate students in the lab, which can be intimidating at first due to their deep knowledge in niche fields. However, it's also inspiring to see their passion and dedication. One PhD student is developing a machine learning algorithm for on-the-fly compression of large datasets, which can be integrated with our VR platform. This would allow us to display a compressed representation of datasets like climate data, improving real-time performance. Working alongside him and other students provides valuable insights into how theoretical concepts are applied in real-world scenarios. Spontaneous brainstorming sessions, such as those over coffee in the lab break room, often lead to innovative ideas and solutions.
archival_memory.poster_presentations: I've had the opportunity to present our research through poster presentations at smaller symposiums around campus. It was a great experience that required me to distill complex research into easy-to-understand visuals and talking points. Initially, I was nervous about facing tough questions from professors or industry professionals. However, the reality was quite different. People were genuinely interested in our work and engaged in friendly dialogues. I even met a few folks from local startups who shared interesting perspectives on how VR for data visualization could benefit commercial industries. It was eye-opening to see how research can transition from academia to real-world applications.
archival_memory.publications: I've been fortunate enough to be a co-author on two workshop papers and am currently working on a larger conference submission for the IEEE Visualization Conference. Our research focuses on comparing traditional 2D dashboards with an interactive VR environment in terms of user performance. We conducted a user study with 15 participants, recording their times and gathering UX feedback. Now, we're analyzing the data to determine if there's a statistically significant difference. Writing the paper is a collaborative effort, with different team members handling different sections. It's a balancing act, especially with senior coursework and a capstone project to manage.
archival_memory.grad_school_plans: I'm currently considering working in the industry for a couple of years before deciding if I want to pursue a master's or PhD. I'm drawn to the idea of contributing to cutting-edge knowledge in areas like data visualization or machine learning. However, I also want to see how these concepts are applied in real product development. My mentor suggested that industry experience can provide a better understanding of relevant problems, which would be beneficial if I decide to return for a PhD with a more practical approach.
archival_memory.frustrations_in_research: Research can be frustrating at times. You may spend weeks on an approach that doesn't pan out or discover that your idea has already been done and improved upon by others. However, the key is to adapt and incorporate the existing knowledge into your work. By reading the existing paper, incorporating their findings, and finding a new angle or application, you can push the boundaries of research. The sense of collaboration within the lab and among the global research community is truly special.
archival_memory.lab_crisis: A few months ago, one of our massive servers crashed, and we lost vital data that wasn't fully backed up. It was a frantic night with email chains and Zoom calls to try and recover the data. Although we managed to restore most of it, the crisis highlighted the importance of data backups. We learned from the experience and set up a better backup system to prevent such a disaster in the future. It was stressful, but it also brought the lab together and taught us valuable lessons.
archival_memory.research_connections: Research has allowed me to connect with professors on a more personal level, beyond just being a student in their classes. My PI is very approachable and supportive, and I can easily reach out to her for guidance on career direction or help with academic struggles. She has also been recommending me for various scholarships, events, and networking opportunities. I had the chance to attend a virtual workshop on immersive analytics, where I met academic experts from around the world. Witnessing their debates on technical details, proposing new frameworks, and seeing them engage in friendly rivalries over theories was truly fascinating. It felt like I was at the forefront of CS knowledge, watching it unfold in real time.
archival_memory.research_journey: My research journey so far has been a mix of hard work, chaos, and rewards. I love the feeling that what I do in the lab might shape the way scientists understand their data in the future. The VR and immersive work we're pioneering could become standard tools one day, and I'd be proud to have been part of it from the beginning. The sense of contributing to something bigger keeps me motivated. This experience has changed how I think about computer science, innovation, and teamwork. I'm grateful for the opportunities I've had and the people I've met along the way.

As a fourth-year Computer Science student, I’ve definitely seen how the culture has evolved over the years, and I’ve discovered a bunch of different communities that make this place feel like a second home. You’d be surprised how many ways there are to get involved beyond just coding in front of your laptop all day.

archival_memory.user_future_plans: I'm currently leaning towards going into the industry for 5 years after graduation. However, I haven't completely ruled out the possibility of attending grad school in the future.
archival_memory.user_job_market_goals: I'm aiming for software engineering roles that overlap with my passions for data visualization, VR/AR technologies, and data-driven product development. I'm drawn to tech companies that push boundaries in data analytics or immersive technologies, such as Unity, Unreal, or specialized VR startups. While big names like Google, Amazon, and Facebook are tempting, I'm also considering smaller companies where I can have a bigger impact earlier on.
archival_memory.user_job_search_process: I'm currently in the midst of campus recruiting, with career fairs and a flurry of applications for software engineering and data engineering roles. Last summer, I interned at a tech startup specializing in data analytics software for logistics companies. That experience was invaluable as I saw how a real development team operates, from planning sprints to handling feature rollouts. My tasks included building UI components and writing data pipelines. By the end of the internship, I felt more confident in my skills, which I believe will help me stand out during interviews.
archival_memory.user_grad_school_considerations: I'm intrigued by the idea of continuing my research in immersive analytics or human-computer interaction for large datasets. Advanced degrees can open doors to specialized R&D roles in industry labs or academia. I enjoy exploring a single topic deeply and pushing the needle forward. However, I also want to apply my knowledge in a commercial setting before committing to a PhD. Some peers suggest doing a part-time master's while working, while others recommend going all-in if I decide to pursue a graduate degree. It's a tough decision to make.
archival_memory.user_club_projects_influence: My involvement in campus clubs and projects has significantly shaped my future aspirations. Through group-driven assignments, such as my current capstone project analyzing social media sentiment for emergency responses, I've realized the value of teamwork and problem-solving in high-stakes scenarios. I thrive on collaborating with others, brainstorming solutions, and iterating until they work. I'm drawn to companies that encourage cross-functional collaboration with designers, data scientists, product managers, and domain experts. The interdisciplinary vibe I've enjoyed in my research lab is something I desire in my professional life as well.
archival_memory.user_financial_considerations: Financial considerations are important for me. I have student loans and want a stable income soon after graduation to pay them off. A full-time engineering position typically offers a decent salary, which would help me quickly eliminate my debt. Additionally, I'm concerned about health insurance and saving for the future. While I'm interested in furthering my education through grad school, I'm aware that funding can be unpredictable, with some programs offering stipends and others requiring tuition payments. Having a good job in industry could provide financial stability and career momentum, allowing me to reassess my desire for further education.
archival_memory.user_interview_preparation: I'm currently focused on staying on top of deadlines and preparing for technical interviews. I set aside time each week to practice problems, brush up on coding patterns, and revisit data structures and algorithms. While I don't love the interview grind, I understand its purpose. The advanced courses I'm taking, such as Advanced Algorithms and Distributed Systems, have significantly boosted my confidence for those tech screens. I feel more comfortable discussing topics like concurrency, big-O notation, and analyzing architecture trade-offs. It's great to see how my coursework is directly benefiting my interview preparation.
archival_memory.user_job_opportunities: I've received initial chats from a few companies, which is surreal considering I still feel like a student. I'm trying to stay grounded and remember that recruiter messages are just the beginning of the hiring process. I'm also exploring smaller companies or startups in my city or nearby tech hubs, as they often offer more hands-on roles where you can learn from day one. The idea of joining a brand-new VR startup, having a stake in its success, and building a product from scratch is incredibly appealing to my entrepreneurial side. I'm excited to see where these opportunities take me.
archival_memory.user_entrepreneurial_aspirations: I've considered launching my own venture, possibly after gaining industry experience. I've had ideas for VR-based training simulators or interactive data analytics platforms. Teaming up with talented friends from my advanced classes or the research lab could make this feasible. However, I'm aware of the challenges and financial risks involved in maintaining a startup. My parents have been supportive but also emphasize the importance of financial independence. I'm taking a thoughtful approach, weighing the pros and cons before making a decision.
archival_memory.user_location_considerations: I'm considering the importance of location in my job search. While I'm open to relocating, I also value being close to my family, who live in a different state. I'm keeping an eye on tech hubs like Silicon Valley, Seattle, Austin, and Midwest cities. The rise of remote or hybrid roles has made it possible to balance career aspirations with personal preferences. I'm excited about the flexibility these options offer, allowing me to potentially work for a big name or innovative startup while living near family or in a location that suits me best. It's a great time to be entering the tech workforce, with many options available.
archival_memory.user_growth_mindset: I'm committed to continuous growth and avoiding stagnation in my career. Even if I don't land in a role that's perfect, as long as I'm learning new skills and approaches, I'll consider it a success. My goal is to become a specialist in immersive tech for data and carve out a niche for myself. To achieve this, I'll stay curious, push my boundaries, and explore different opportunities. I'm excited about the potential paths ahead and looking forward to seeing how things unfold after graduation.
